name: 一蘭 新宿中央東口店
address_ja: 〒160-0022 東京都新宿区新宿3-34-11 ピースビル B1F
cuisine: One dish only, eaten alone: Hakata tonkotsu ramen in a partitioned solo booth, ordered on a paper sheet where you set broth richness, garlic, spring onion, pork and the house red chilli paste — about ¥1,180 for the standard bowl, ¥210 for a kaedama refill, open around the clock with a late-night surcharge from 22:00
neighborhood: Shinjuku 3-chōme, in a basement just east of Shinjuku Station — 3 min from Shinjuku Station (JR Yamanote, Chūō, Sōbu; Odakyū; Keiō) and 3 min from Shinjuku-sanchōme (Tokyo Metro Marunouchi and Fukutoshin, Toei Shinjuku lines)
hours_raw: 24時間営業／年中無休 ※営業時間は状況により急遽変更する場合がございます。22:00〜6:00は深夜料金
gf_detail: Ichiran's own allergen table marks 小麦 (wheat) as present in every noodle it serves, including the standard 天然とんこつラーメン, and the same page carries the chain's blanket cross-contact disclaimer: 「製造・店舗での調理の際には細心の注意を払っておりますが、他のアレルギー物質が微量混入する場合がございます」, followed by 「心配な場合は専門医にご相談のうえお客様ご自身でご判断くださいますようお願いいたします」. There is no gluten-free noodle, no dedicated pot, and no statement anywhere that the chain can accommodate a wheat allergy. The soup itself declares soy rather than wheat, but the noodles alone rule the dish out. A celiac should not eat here.
vegan_detail: The entire menu is built on 天然とんこつ — a pork-bone broth — with pork chāshū as the standard topping. No vegan or vegetarian bowl is offered at the shop (the chain's separate No-Pork retail pack is a mail-order product, not a branch menu item).

chef_bio.background: Not a chef-led restaurant: 一蘭 is a Fukuoka-born tonkotsu specialist that serves a single ramen and nothing else, and the Shinjuku Chūō-Higashiguchi branch is one of three Ichiran shops around Shinjuku Station (the others being 西新宿店 and 新宿歌舞伎町店). The chain's identity rests on its 味集中カウンター — the partitioned 'flavour-concentration counter' where a bamboo blind lifts, an order sheet is passed through, and the diner never sees the staff — which it lists among its five self-declared firsts. This branch is counter-only, 28 seats, no tables and no private room.
chef_bio.philosophy: Eat the bowl alone and undistracted; every variable on the order sheet is the diner's to set.
chef_bio.specialty: 天然とんこつラーメン with the 秘伝のたれ red chilli paste; kaedama noodle refills.
chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: The chain's own branch page ichiran.com/shop/tokyo/shinjuku/ gives 〒160-0022 東京都新宿区新宿3-34-11 ピースビルB1F, 24-hour opening, 28 counter seats, no parking, a 22:00–6:00 late-night surcharge, and links to the allergen sheet at ichiran.com/ramen/allergie.html. Tabelog's detail page (tokyo/A1304/A130401/13100501) carries the same address with coordinates 35.690594 / 139.702815, 営業時間 24時間営業・年中無休, a ¥1,000–¥1,999 band and access of 3 min from both Shinjuku and Shinjuku-sanchōme stations. Gnavi lists the same shop as 一蘭 新宿中央東口店, 地下鉄丸ノ内線新宿三丁目駅 徒歩2分. A Gnavi full-text search on 一蘭 新宿 returns exactly three shops — 新宿歌舞伎町店, 西新宿店 and 新宿中央東口店 — confirming there is no separate 新宿東口店.

gf_cross_contamination: Wheat noodles are boiled in the same water all day and the shop serves nothing that is not built on them; there is no separate pot or fryer line to ask for.
The chain's allergen page states plainly that trace amounts of other allergens may get in during manufacture and in-store preparation, and puts the final judgement on the customer.
soy_sauce_wheat: The broth's declared allergen is soy; the noodles carry the wheat. Either way the dish cannot be made wheat-free.
vegan_cross_contact: Single pork-bone broth for the whole menu; nothing on the premises is animal-free.
staff_allergy_handling: Orders are placed on a paper sheet through a blind and staff are largely unseen, so there is no natural moment to discuss an allergy; the chain publishes an allergen table instead of offering accommodation.
positives: A full allergen table is published per product on the official site, which is more than most ramen shops offer.
Solo booths, an English-capable paper order sheet and 24-hour opening make it one of the least socially demanding meals in Shinjuku — for anyone who can eat wheat.

cultural_comfort.note: The booth format removes almost all social friction: you buy a ticket, fill in a multilingual order sheet, sit in a partitioned stall and never have to speak. Open 24 hours, three minutes from either station, no reservation. The catch is that it is wheat from end to end, so it belongs in the app as a clearly-labelled no for gluten rather than as an option.
